title.narrative: FAO/UN Environment Partnership for Marine Coastal Governance and Fisheries
FAO/UN Environment Partnership for Marine Coastal Governance and Fisheries

description.narrative:
FAO ämnar att ingå i ett gemensamt projekt med UN Environment för att adressera gemensamma utmaningar avseende marin miljö och fiske i västra Indiska Oceanen. Samarbetet kommer att ske mellan organisationernas respektive institutioner ansvariga för fiske (South West Indian Ocean Fisheries Commission) och marin miljö (Nairobikonventionen). Projeketet planeras att pågå mellan 2018-2023. Sverige är för tillfället ensam givare till projektet med ett totalt bidrag om 79 miljoner kronor. Avtalet med FAO kommer att kompletteras med ett avtal mellan de de två deltagande organisationerna där FAO kommer att vidarebeforda medel till UN Environment.
Projektets mål är att stärka samarbete runt fiskeförvaltning och marina resurser. Genom de två deltagande organisationerna kommer insatsen arbeta på både regional och nationell nivå i och mellan de länder som tillhör South West Indian Ocean Fisheries Commission och Nairobikonventionen (Komorerna, Kenya, Madagascar, Mauritius, Maldiverna, Mozambique, Seychellerna, Somalia, Sydafrika, Tanzania and Yemen). Genom att stärka samarbetet mellan fiskesektorn och miljösektorn förväntas projeketet bidra till det övergripande målet att nå en ekologiskt och ekonomiskt hållbar tillväxt i regionen, med ett särskilt fokus på kustområden och fiskebefolkningen. Projeketet är organiserat i 3 komponenter. En del som främst riktar sig mot att stärka miljöförvaltningen på regional och nationell nivå, en del som riktar sig mot att utveckla fiskeförvaltning med ett integrerart hållbarhets- och ekologiskt perspektiv, och slutligen en del för förbättra samarbetet mellan de båda sektorerna på nationell och regional nivå.

The FAO aims to enter into a joint project with UN Environment to address common challenges regarding marine environment and fisheries in the Western Indian Ocean. The implementation will be carried out jointly by the respective institutions of South West Indian Ocean Fisheries Commission and the Nairobi Convention. The project is scheduled to last between 2018-2023. Sweden is currently the only donor of the project with a total contribution of SEK 79 million. The agreement with the FAO will be complemented by an inter-agency agreement between the two participating organizations.
The project's main objective is to strengthen cooperation around fisheries management and marine environment. Through the two participating organizations, the project will work at both regional and national levels. The following countries are members/signatories of the South West Indian Ocean Fisheries Commission and the Nairobi Convention: Comoros, Kenya, Madagascar, Mauritius, Maldives, Mozambique, Seychelles, Somalia, South Africa, Tanzania and Yemen. By strengthening cooperation between the fisheries sector and the environmental sector, the project is expected to contribute to improve food security, increase resilience, and reduce poverty of youth, women and men in coastal communities, and particularly fishing communities. The project is organized into 3 components/outcomes: Outcome/Component 1: Resilience of livelihoods based on WIO marine and coastal ecosystem and habitats enhanced Outcome/Component 2: Coastal fisheries are sustainably managed using the Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries and livelihoods options enhanced Outcome/Component 3: Cooperation and coordination between fisheries and environmental management institutions and field interventions enhanced

The intervention has three interrelated outcome objectives: 1. Resilience of livelihoods based on Western Indian Ocean marine and coastal ecosystem and habitats enhanced. 2. Coastal fisheries in the Western Indian Ocean are sustainably managed using the Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries and livelihoods options enhanced. 3. Cooperation and coordination between fisheries and environmental management institutions and field interventions in the Western Indian Ocean is enhanced. These results are ultimately contributing to the long-term impact objective: To improve food security, increase resilience, and reduce poverty of youth, women and men in coastal communities, and particularly fishing communities, in the Western Indian Ocean region.

While the agreement between Sida and FAO was signed in December 2018. The project have had a long preparation phase and it was only during 2020 activities started to any larger extent. During 2021 the implementation activities has picked up in pace but progress is still a bit slow. The delays in implementing can be explained by two main reasons: - The time needed to formalise the inter-agency agreement between FAO and UN Environment. In the absence of this agreement, both recruitments and actual activities were suspended. - Difficulties in recruiting key personnel for the project has been another main reason for delays. It was first during 2021 the project was fully staffed and physically working from Maputo. -As a consequence of the reasons mentioned above, the agreements with the Lead National Authorities for fisheries and environment was also delayed.
SWIOFC and NC has now clarified the implementation arrangements and an inception report with up- dated work plan as well as budget has been discussed and agreed up on among the partners. However up to this date the final approved versions has not yet been submitted to Sida.
Annual review meeting combined with first Project Steering Committee was held in July 2021.
Now with all formalities and staff in place the pre-conditions for improved implementation pace is there.
In 2021 as well as in 2020, COVID-19 has led to additional slowdown of some of the planned activities. It has also led to some shifts in approaches, such moving away from using international experts to using more local experts compered to original plans.
In spite of the challenges with formalities, staff recruitment and COVID 19, implementing activates has been prepared for and in some cases taking place in parallel. With the delays in mind, there are few substantial results to report and the ones achieved are more related to planning and output level rather than upper level outcomes.
Below are examples of results:
1. Enhanced resilience of livelihoods based on Western Indian Ocean marine and coastal ecosystem and habitats:
-SWIOFC and NC has clarifying implementation arrangements. A regional project inception workshop was conducted in May 2021. A draft inception report with up- dated workplan as well as budget was discussed at the 1st Project Steering Committee meeting in June and agreed up on among the partners during second part of the year. However at this date the approved versions has not yet been submitted.
-The project have had joint planning meetings with national institutions and authorities to create national ownership and engagement in the project and to enable to demonstrate seamless collaboration and build long term capacity and understanding of the collaborative approaches.
2. Fisheries Management-Environmental Policy Dialogue is being established and operational at regional and national levels.
-Three pilot countries have been selected for implementation national level interventions of the project; namely Madagascar, Mozambique and Tanzania, selection of specific sites in respectively country has been done, based on common agreed criterias and operational structures are being developed with the three national teams compost of National focal points and technical experts from environment and fisheries agencies.
-Baseline studies has been conducted for Mozambique and Tanzania and are planned for Madagascar towards end of the year.
-Key policy recommendations from the NC-SPP of relevance to fisheries were presented to the SWIOFC Scientific Committee 2 June 2021 as part of furthering exchange between the two advisory frameworks.
3. Cooperation and coordination between fisheries and environmental management institutions and field interventions in the Western Indian Ocean is enhanced.
-The Regional Project Management Unit (RPMU) is now complete with the recruitment of a Chief Technical Adviser and appointment of an Environmental Management Expert and a Fisheries Management Expert. Arrangements for the development and follow up of an M&E framework for the project and technical support in building synergies with relevant initiatives in the region and globally are in place.
-National Inter-ministerial Project Steering Committees have been established to serve as platforms for national consultations to discuss participatory and evidence-based processes to link fisheries and environment and address joint issues to be identified at the regional level.
- Except for getting the administrative formalities and routines in place, focus has been on developing criterias and methodologies to be used and tested in the case studies. Harmonized approaches has been developed for a number of topics, such as ecosystem valuation and financial analysis, climate, blue economy.
- A plan for capturing of lessons learned and best practice and development of M&E plan has been initiated by M&E expert.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
